headline: SIGN AFTER CHANGES: 10 blockers across liability, IP, and client flowdown terms

findings.title: Missing requirement to obtain client's prior consent for subcontracting
findings.impact: AtliQ would be in non-compliance with its client commitments by engaging the subcontractor without securing prior written consent.

citations.docTitle: Kriti Data Labs subcontractor agreement (AtliQ draft)
citations.quote: Vendor shall not subcontract any portion of the Services without AtliQ's prior written consent
Supplier may subcontract parts of the services only with Client's prior written consent

findings.standard: Apply the same standard AtliQ asks for as a supplier: capped penalties or none, 30-day pay, mutual caps, no pay-when-paid, fair termination. Pass the client's obligations down (IP, confidentiality, data protection, consent), never the client's leverage.
findings.counterPosition: Add a condition precedent stating that the agreement is contingent upon AtliQ obtaining prior written consent from the End Client.

precedents.label: standard

findings.title: Missing data processing agreement and personnel training flowdowns
findings.impact: AtliQ will be in non-compliance with its GDPR obligations under the client contract to ensure subcontractors are bound to a DPA and properly trained.

citations.docTitle: Kriti Data Labs subcontractor agreement (AtliQ draft)
citations.quote: Source data comprises vibration, temperature and pressure sensor streams from End Client customer plants, together with maintenance work orders and technician logs (including technician names, shift identifiers and free-text notes). Vendor Personnel shall access data via AtliQ-provisioned cloud workspaces and Vendor's own labelling platform

To the extent Supplier processes personal data on behalf of Client, the Parties shall conclude the Data Processing Agreement pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR attached as **Annex 3**, which forms an integral part of this Agreement.
13.2 Transfers of personal data to India shall be based on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Module 2, Controller-to-Processor) incorporated in Annex 3, supplemented by the technical and organisational measures described therein.
13.3 Supplier shall ensure that its personnel are bound to confidentiality and data secrecy and receive appropriate data protection training

findings.standard: DPA (EU) or BAA (US health) signed before any personal/regulated data moves, with a sub-DPA / sub-BAA for every party that touches the data (incl. AtliQ's own Pune entity); engagement-specific scope; offshore access only as the agreement allows.
findings.counterPosition: Execute a back-to-back Data Processing Agreement (DPA) incorporating EU Standard Contractual Clauses, and require the vendor to ensure all personnel receive appropriate data protection training and are bound by confidentiality.

7.1 If the Service Provider fails to complete a Milestone by the agreed date for reasons solely attributable to the Service Provider, the Service Provider shall pay liquidated damages at the rate of 0.5% (half percent) of the Milestone Fee of the delayed Milestone for each complete week of delay.

7.2 The aggregate liquidated damages in respect of any Milestone shall not exceed 5% (five percent) of the Milestone Fee of that Milestone.

7.3 No liquidated damages shall be payable where the delay is caused by the Client, including delayed access to data or systems, delayed review of Deliverables, or changes in scope, or by a Force Majeure event.

7.4 The Parties agree that the liquidated damages are a genuine pre-estimate of loss and shall be the Client's sole and exclusive remedy for delay.
hits.differs: Increases rate to 2% daily from 0.5% weekly; removes 5% cap and client-delay exclusions.

hits.heading: DELIVERY, ACCEPTANCE AND LIQUIDATED DAMAGES
hits.label: exception
hits.labelNote: One-off: "strategic exception for Al Noor only, not our new standard" (cap 10% of total fees)
hits.text:
10.1 The Supplier shall use all reasonable endeavours to achieve each Milestone by the date set out in the relevant SOW.

10.2 Each Deliverable shall be subject to acceptance testing by the Client within ten (10) Business Days of delivery against the acceptance criteria in the SOW. Deliverables not rejected in writing within that period shall be deemed accepted.

10.3 If the Supplier fails to achieve a Milestone by its due date for reasons attributable to the Supplier, the Supplier shall pay to the Client, as liquidated damages, one percent (1%) of the Fees payable for the affected Milestone for each complete week of delay, provided that the aggregate liquidated damages payable under this Agreement shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the total Fees payable under this Agreement.

10.4 The Parties agree that the liquidated damages in Clause 10.3 are a genuine pre-estimate of loss. No liquidated damages shall be payable for delay caused by the Client, its contractors, or a Force Majeure Event.
hits.differs: Increases rate to 2% of total fees daily; removes milestone-specific calculation and excludes acceptance period.

hits.label: untagged
hits.text:
15.1 This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of India.

15.2 Disputes not resolved by negotiation between senior management within thirty (30) days shall be referred to arbitration by a sole arbitrator under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. The seat and venue of arbitration shall be Pune, and the language shall be English.

15.1 This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Republic of Singapore.

15.2 The Parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute through good-faith discussions between senior executives for thirty (30) days.

15.3 Any dispute not so resolved shall be referred to and finally resolved by arbitration administered by the Singapore International Arbitration Centre ("**SIAC**") under the SIAC Rules in force at the time. The seat of arbitration shall be Singapore. The tribunal shall consist of one (1) arbitrator. The language of arbitration shall be English.
hits.differs: Changes governing law and seat from Singapore/SIAC to India and Pune courts; shorter escalation.
